headline_marked: [[Google rolls out advanced Android sideloading]] for power users, bypassing ADB
headline: Google rolls out advanced Android sideloading for power users, bypassing ADB
summary: Google is beginning to roll out an advanced sideloading flow, allowing power users to install apps from unverified developers on certified Android devices without needing ADB. This comes ahead of a global developer verification system set for 2027.
details: Google has started implementing its advanced sideloading flow on Android, enabling power users to install apps from unverified developers on certified devices without using ADB. This marks a significant change in how sideloading will function on the platform.

This new system is part of Google's broader initiative, launched in March, requiring developers to verify their identities. The goal is to tie all apps, including sideloaded ones, to a verified developer ID to enhance accountability and combat malware distribution.

To utilize the advanced flow, users must first activate a toggle within the hidden Developer options menu. They then need to authenticate their identity, restart their device, and observe a 24-hour waiting period before proceeding to sideload apps from unverified sources.

Even after enabling the advanced flow, Android will display a warning each time an app from an unverified developer is installed or updated. Users can, however, bypass this warning by tapping the "Install anyway" button.
The process is intentionally complex to deter regular users from inadvertently installing malicious applications. Google aims to strike a balance between user freedom and security.

For power users, the good news is that the advanced sideloading flow only needs to be enabled once. Google will automatically remember this choice across all their certified devices. Users can still sideload via ADB if they choose not to enable the advanced flow.

The rollout is gradual, meaning it might not appear on all phones immediately. The feature relies on a new "Android Developer Verifier" system service, which can be manually installed from the Play Store to potentially expedite access.
Google's app verification system will initially begin verifying app installations from specific app stores starting September 30, 2026. This phased approach allows for testing and refinement.

The full app verification system will be enforced for Android users in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand this year. It is slated for a global expansion to all certified Android devices in 2027.

headline_marked: [[Apple pulls AI ‘nudify’ app]] promoted in Meta ads
headline: Apple pulls AI ‘nudify’ app promoted in Meta ads
summary: The app, promoted via Meta ads, allowed users to create AI-generated pornographic deepfakes, including one resembling a prominent US politician.
details: Apple has removed an AI-powered "nudify" app from its App Store after it was found to generate pornographic deepfakes. The controversial application had been actively promoted through advertisements on Meta's platforms.

The app allowed users to create explicit images of real people using artificial intelligence. One specific instance highlighted involved a deepfake featuring a woman who strongly resembled a well-known US politician.

The incident raises significant concerns about content moderation policies on both app stores and advertising platforms. Both Apple and Meta face scrutiny over the presence and promotion of such potentially harmful AI tools.
